anomalies.observed: On the FCC Peripherals sheet the PCA9685PW (U2) address-select pins A0..A5 (pins 1,2,3,4,5,24) are all tied to the GND net, and the annotation beside the part reads 'I2C address: 0x41'. The INA219 (U1) is wired on the same I2C2 bus (SDA/SCL = I2C2_SDA_FCC/I2C2_SCL_FCC) with its address pins grounded, i.e. 0x40.
anomalies.expected: To realise the annotated 0x41 only A0 should be pulled high with A1..A5 low; with every address pin grounded the PCA9685 answers at 0x40, which is already the address of the INA219 on the same I2C2 bus, so the two devices must not share 0x40.

evidence.quote: I2C address: 0x41 (FCCPeripherals sheet, 'PWM Driver' block, U2 PCA9685PW)
PWM/servo driver | FCCPeripherals | NXP PCA9685PW (I2C 16-ch PWM), I2C addr 0x40
Current/voltage sensor | Hades (top sheet) | TI INA219AIDCNR, I2C addr 0x40, across R1 = 10 mΩ shunt

anomalies.impact: The 16-channel PWM driver and the current/voltage monitor would both respond at 0x40 on I2C2. Transactions addressed to the servo driver would also be accepted by the INA219 (and vice versa), producing corrupted power/current telemetry and unpredictable servo/PWM outputs.

parsed.summary: A discrepancy exists on the FCC peripheral bus: the PCA9685's address annotation says 0x41, but its A0..A5 pins appear tied to GND, which would put it at 0x40 — the same address as the INA219 already on I2C2 — so the two devices would collide. The finding is reported at low confidence because the address-pin wiring is hard to read and the spec itself lists the PCA9685 as 0x40.
